You have been paged. It is 2026-11-16 05:20:55 UTC.

Alerts firing in namespace testbed (1):

1. CacheHitRatioLow (severity: ticket)
   Fewer than 20% of inventory stock lookups are served from the cache.
   labels: {}
   condition true since: 05:18:46 UTC
   rule: sum(rate(inventory_cache_requests_total{result="hit"}[2m])) / sum(rate(inventory_cache_requests_total[2m])) < 0.2

Investigate, then file the incident report with submit_report.

submission.summary: The cache hit ratio fell to 0% at about 05:18 because Redis's runtime maxmemory was lowered from 64 MB to 1 MB (1048576 bytes) with CONFIG SET at 05:17:23. Redis already held about 1.44 MB, so it rejects writes with OOM. Inventory-service therefore serves every stock lookup from Postgres, and the cache cannot be refilled. The user-facing impact so far is extra Postgres load and latency; gateway 5xx rates are back to 0 after an earlier node-not-ready incident (04:51-05:12), which is a separate, already-recovered event.

root_causes.explanation: The running Redis instance has maxmemory = 1 MB, set at runtime by CONFIG SET maxmemory 1048576 at 05:17:23. The deployment still specifies --maxmemory 64mb, so the live value differs from the spec. Redis's data set (about 1.44 MB) is above the new ceiling, so writes fail with 'OOM command not allowed'. inventory-service logs 'cache write failed' for every miss, and cache reads return nothing, so every stock lookup falls through to Postgres and the hit ratio drops to 0.

evidence.finding: inventory_cache_requests_total rate: hit went from about 4 req/s to 0 at 05:18; miss rose from about 2.6 to about 7 req/s at 05:17-05:18. Error results 05:06-05:10 are from the earlier node incident.
inventory-service logs repeated WARN 'cache write failed' with err 'OOM command not allowed when used memory > maxmemory' from 05:20 onward, on both inventory pods.
redis deployment (revision 1, created 2026-11-10, unchanged) runs redis:7.4.5-alpine with args --maxmemory 64mb --maxmemory-policy allkeys-lru, so the spec does not explain the 1 MB value.
redis_config_maxmemory was 67108864 (64 MB) through 05:09 and became 1048576 (1 MB) by 05:21.

Redis log at 05:17:23: 'WARNING: the new maxmemory value set via CONFIG SET (1048576) is smaller than the current memory usage (1439032)'. The pod was not restarted (it started 04:42:45), so the change came from a runtime CONFIG SET.

redis_commands cmd=config|set went to 0 rate at 05:18:16 after the earlier set traffic, consistent with a single manual CONFIG SET. redis_commands get rate stayed about 7/s, and redis_memory_used_bytes stayed about 1.44 MB.
Gateway 5xx ratio is 0 from 05:13 to 05:21. The earlier spike (04:59-05:12, up to 26%) is the node-not-ready incident, now recovered. No user-facing errors are linked to the cache change yet.

timeline.event: redis pod started with --maxmemory 64mb (restart count from the earlier node incident)
CONFIG SET maxmemory 1048576 (1 MB) applied to the running redis, below its 1.44 MB usage; Redis warns about it
config|set traffic seen in redis_commands; inventory cache hit rate drops to 0
inventory-service logs 'cache write failed: OOM command not allowed' (ongoing)
restart_pod on redis-7d9d88cc-lnhpm proposed (not executed): it is the only redis replica, so it needs human approval

recommended_actions.rationale: Restore the runtime maxmemory to the spec value 64mb, either with CONFIG SET maxmemory 67108864 on the running redis (keeps the data) or by restarting the pod, which reloads --maxmemory 64mb from the deployment args. The restart proposal (restart_pod on redis-7d9d88cc-lnhpm) is pending human approval because redis has a single replica. Afterwards, confirm redis_config_maxmemory = 67108864, inventory cache writes succeed, and the hit ratio returns to about 80%+. Also find out who ran CONFIG SET, and consider blocking runtime CONFIG changes (rename-command CONFIG) or alerting on redis_config_maxmemory drift from the spec.

input.reason: Redis maxmemory was lowered at runtime via CONFIG SET to 1048576 (1 MB) at 05:17:23 (call c10 log: 'new maxmemory value set via CONFIG SET (1048576) is smaller than current memory usage (1439032)'; call c9 shows redis_config_maxmemory went 67108864 -> 1048576 at 05:21). Deployment args still say --maxmemory 64mb (call c8). inventory-service cache writes fail with OOM (call c4), hit ratio dropped to 0 (call c1). Restarting the pod resets the runtime config to the 64mb from the deployment args.

actions.reason: recorded for a human operator; not executed
actions.summary: delete pod/redis-7d9d88cc-lnhpm so that deployment/redis replaces it with a new pod
actions.risk_reason: this is the only available replica: the component is down until its replacement is ready
